title: Five ways to give someone your attention
description: Small, ordinary invitations to be a little more present.

body.heading: Make a little space
paragraphs: 1. Ask whether now is a good time. Attention is easier to offer when both people can choose the moment. “Would you like to talk?” leaves room for a yes, a no, or a later.
2. Put one distraction aside. You might silence your own phone or turn away from a screen, if doing so is practical. Do not demand that someone else do the same.

body.heading: Let the other person lead
paragraphs: 3. Ask an open question. “What was the interesting part?” can invite a fuller answer than a rapid series of guesses. Let silence be part of the conversation.
4. Check what you heard. Try “Have I understood that correctly?” rather than assuming you know how someone feels. People can correct your understanding in their own words.

body.heading: Finish thoughtfully
paragraphs: 5. Ask what would be useful. Someone may want company, an idea, practical help, or simply to finish a sentence. Accept their answer, including a wish for space.
These are everyday conversation suggestions, not therapy or a promise to repair a relationship. Your own boundaries matter too. You can offer attention without agreeing to do everything asked of you.

takeaway: Ask, listen, check your understanding, and respect the other person’s choice.
